original.target_description: Body sway and heart rate (freezing-response measures) when viewing angry, socially threatening faces. Roelofs et al. (2010), Study 1; precise target test unresolved.

n.sample_role: Female participants; initial included sample reported, final critical-test analytic count unresolved.
n.exclusions: Three body-sway outliers identified (Z scores greater than 4); exclusion/final count not explicitly stated.
n.location: Printed pp. 1576–1577 (PDF pp. 2–3), Participants and opening Results; critical results pp. 1577, 1579.
n.quote: Fifty female students (mean age = 20.6 years, SD = 2.3 years) ... were included in this study. ... Three participants were identified as outliers because of their ... excessive movements, as reflected in Z scores greater than 4 ... on the body-sway measure.

es.location: Printed p. 1579 (PDF p. 5), Heart rate continuation; body-sway results on printed p. 1577 (PDF p. 3).
es.quote: Finally, there was a positive correlation between heart rate ... and body sway in the angry-faces block (r = .29, p = .048), and ... this indicated that immobility was related to bradycardia in the ... social threat condition.

p.location: Printed p. 1579 (PDF p. 5), Heart rate continuation; body-sway results on printed p. 1577 (PDF p. 3).
p.quote: Finally, there was a positive correlation between heart rate ... and body sway in the angry-faces block (r = .29, p = .048), and ... this indicated that immobility was related to bradycardia in the ... social threat condition.

notes:
Only assigned unfinished fields checked; all other fields/sides are placeholders. Published title and authors match the reference. Rendered PDF pages 2–5 inspected.
The Participants section reports 50 female students included; the opening Results identifies three excessive-movement outliers but does not explicitly state their exclusion or the final analytic N for the critical test. No mutually exclusive final groups are printed. Recruitment N is not substituted, and N is not inferred from degrees of freedom.
At PDF p. 5 (printed p. 1579), angry-block heart-rate/body-sway correlation is a strong candidate: printed Pearson r=.29, p=.048. However, the description names both freezing measures without specifying correlation versus separate effects of angry faces on each measure. Separate body-sway emotion omnibus (PDF p. 3) F(2,45)=5.20, partial eta-squared=.19, p=.009 and heart-rate angry-versus-happy contrast (PDF p. 5) F(1,45)=6.24, partial eta-squared=.12, p=.016 are distinct candidate tests. No target selected by matching the requested metric. No conversion of Pearson r to partial eta-squared.
No analytic N arithmetic performed; no effect conversion performed.
